{"decision":"`req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` (b) offered exactly two ways out for `disconnected_community`: "Either rename it to what it computes (\"tightly-coupled cluster\") or make it compute what it claims." NEITHER WAS TAKEN. The message was rewritten to describe the walk it actually made, and the category key `disconnected_community` was left alone.

WHY RENAMING LOST. The key is a consumer contract in three places at once: it is a documented HEAL category, it is what `detect_defects` callers match on, and `ility.rs` uses it as a named ility source (`detect_defects.disconnected_community`). Renaming it would break every consumer in order to fix a sentence — the cost lands on people who did nothing wrong, to repair prose they never read. dev_storyflow's fleet matches on these keys.

WHY RECOMPUTING LOST, and this is the one worth reading. "Make it compute what it claims" sounds like the honest option and is the wrong diagnosis: the detector's computation is not broken. It runs connected components over `design_network()`, correctly. THE REQUIREMENT'S OWN TEXT MISDESCRIBES IT AS COMPUTING MODULARITY, WHICH IT DOES NOT. What is narrow is the NETWORK, and the narrowing is deliberate and load-bearing — `NON_DESIGN_TYPES` and the exclusion of `CONTAINS` exist because provenance nodes and decomposition scaffolds distort the topology, each for a reason with its own record (BL-84, BL-124). Making it "compute what it claims" would mean walking the whole graph, which would undo those and report every Fragment as an island. The fix was never in the algorithm.

⭐ SO THE GENERAL FORM, which is why this is a Decision and not a code comment: WHEN A CHECK'S NAME OVERSTATES ITS COMPUTATION, THE THIRD OPTION IS USUALLY RIGHT — leave the identifier, leave the algorithm, and make the OUTPUT state its own scope. A key is an interface; a message is addressed to a reader; only the second is free to change, and only the second was ever wrong.

── A LARGER ROAD NOT TAKEN, recorded because it will be re-proposed ──
The requirement is titled "A report says what it swept", and the fullest reading of that is to change `detect_defects` itself to return `{swept: {...}, defects: [...]}` instead of a bare array — which is what the SCOPED variant already does (`Scoped` carries `total`, `in_scope`, `region_size`, `note`), so the two halves of one tool are inconsistent today and that asymmetry is real.

NOT DONE HERE, on scope rather than on merit. It breaks every consumer that indexes the array, it is a minor version bump, and the requirement's own owed items are enumerated (a), (b), (c) and are all satisfiable without it. The requirement also states its own boundary: "NOT IN SCOPE: whether every reporting tool needs this treatment or only those whose zero is read as permission." Doing the shape change under the cover of finishing (b) and (c) would have been the widening this project keeps warning about.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether the unscoped `detect_defects` should match the scoped one's envelope. That is a genuine open question about surface consistency, and it is Anthony's, not an implementer's.","name":"When a detector's NAME is wrong, fix what it SAYS — the key is a contract and the sentence is not","rationale":"The category key is an interface — matched by callers and used by name as an ility source — while the message is addressed to a reader. Only the message was ever wrong, so only the message changed. "Make it compute what it claims" was rejected on a sharper ground than cost: the computation is correct, and the narrowness people mistake for a bug is the deliberate exclusion of provenance nodes and CONTAINS, each with its own record. Widening the walk would undo BL-84 and BL-124 and report every Fragment as an island.","status":"proposed"}
